data.summary: services/forbidden.py: with a multi-line quote in the command, _split stops treating ; as a separator (a word comes back as `-q;`) and matching only sees the start of each command. F.check returns None for `echo a; git push origin main; python3 -c "<newline>print(1)"`, and the same for `git stash -q` and `pkill x`; the one-line form is refused. Seen for real: sw-waitcycle ran git stash and git stash pop in a worktree unrefused on 2026-11-05 in such a line, then `git stash list` was refused. Its commits hold only its own files, so nothing crossed over. Regression test: those three commands must be refused.
data.title: The forbidden-command guard misses any command after a semicolon when the line holds a multi-line quoted string

data.claim: leasebreak.progress_at plus the live-gate registry and running jobs give a per-lease watermark, so leasewait stays pure (Held.progress_at), the victim is the least-progress holder, and an alarm is a wait older than a knob whose leases in the way all show no work for as long.
data.falsifier: A holder with the older wait but the newer watermark still being chosen as the victim, or a working holder still raising an alarm, or a queue with no wait reading the log.
data.mechanism: Held carries the watermark; find() ranks ring members by it, falling back to the youngest wait on a tie. progress_of is lazy, so it reads the log and git only once a cycle or an aged wait exists.
data.probe: uv run pytest tests/test_wait_cycle_followups.py -q -n 0 --tb=no -k "least_progress or more_active or equal_or_unmeasured or past_the_limit or young_wait or two_waits or every_dropped"
data.question: Can the wait-cycle victim follow progress, and can a stuck wait raise an alarm, from facts ddflow already has, with no new event kind and no cost on a queue with no stuck wait?

evidence.note: R28698d8002 CONFIRMED: 7 probe tests passed. Open reading, for the operator to confirm: 'nothing running' is judged per wait (no live gate, running job or progress on the leases in its way), not project-wide, because with many lanes a project-wide test would never fire. Default wait_alarm_s 1200 is chosen below the default lease.ttl_s 1800, since a wait nobody re-asks lapses at its TTL.

chunk_findings.detail: In `facts`, the `running` generator does `clock.epoch(j.started_at)` for any job with `ended_at` false/`None` and `budget > 0`, before `JOBS.status(j).state == "running"` is checked. A folded state containing a queued job (`started_at=None`, `ended_at=None`) will make the first progress lookup raise `TypeError`/`ValueError` as soon as a cycle or aged wait forces `facts()` to run. The status/doctor report then crashes on a realistic queued-not-started job.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/waitcycles.py:progress_of:facts

chunk_findings.detail: The new code calls `time.time()` directly for `at`/`now` defaults instead of using the clock port required by [r-adapters]. The rule lists clocks among the external dependencies that must go through `ddflow/adapters`; using `time` directly bypasses the injectable clock adapter and violates the project rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/waitcycles.py:progress_of/wait_cycles/wait_alarms

chunk_findings.detail: [Imported `clock` directly from the local `ddflow.core` package instead of a port under `ddflow/adapters`, contrary to [r-adapters]. A clock is explicitly listed as an external dependency that must go through `ddflow/adapters`; this direct import means a fake clock cannot be swapped at the adapter boundary and a clock change must touch this core file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/leasewait.py: from . import clock

chunk_findings.detail: `as_dict()` emits only `self.drops[0].command()` and `self.drops[0].mcp()` even when `self.drops` has more than one `Drop`. A single wait can be blocked on multiple leases held by the least-progress holder (the new `_drop`/`_joined` path can produce multiple `Drop` entries), so an alert/API consumer that follows the returned `command`/`mcp` will run only the first release, leaving the other leases still held and the wait still blocked. Example: one wait is blocked on leases `L1` and `L2`, both held by the victim; `drops == (Drop(L1,...), Drop(L2,...))`, but `as_dict()` returns a command for `L1` only. `render()` already joins every `d.command()`; `as_dict()` should join all of them (or not present a single command as the complete remedy when there is more than one drop).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/leasewait.py:Alarm.as_dict

chunk_findings.detail: These two tests call `run_cli(repo, "brief", ...)` and assert the brief output contains `- lease deadlock: agent-a -> agent-b -> agent-a` and `- lease wait alarm: agent-a on T1`. But the intent for this change explicitly says “The brief surface and the lanes advisor wiring are held by other lanes and land later,” and the manifest for this change contains no brief CLI change. The existing brief command will not emit those lines, so `test_the_brief_names_a_deadlock` and `test_the_brief_raises_the_alarm` fail when run against this change as delivered.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_cycle_followups.py:286-300

chunk_findings.detail: `progress_of` documents that it reads nothing until `progress` is first asked, so a queue with no stuck wait pays no git or log read. `act = activity or LB.tree_activity(log.root)` runs at construction, and `wait_report` always constructs this before `wait_cycles` / `wait_alarms`. With no `lease.waiting` rows and `activity=None`, doctor/status still call `LB.tree_activity` (and again if a caller passes a falsy measured activity such as `{}`). A tree walk that raises then fails the report even though no watermark is ever needed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/waitcycles.py:30

chunk_findings.detail: `Drop.command` and `Drop.mcp` join `keep` with commas and interpolate the result unquoted. Given `keep=("src/my file.py",)` (or any glob containing a comma), `command()` returns `ddflow update ITEM --globs src/my file.py`, which a shell splits into two arguments, and `mcp()` emits `globs=src/my file.py`, so the suggested remedy does not preserve the globs the cycle computed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/leasewait.py:Drop.command
